findings.failure_path: A pull request can retain the existing required job but remove this step, replace its command with a no-op, or weaken the candidate-owned gate/validator. The job then succeeds without comparing the landing candidate to review evidence, so the fact that editing the workflow would have changed the candidate hash provides no protection—the check responsible for detecting that change no longer runs honestly.
findings.smallest_fix: Run this assertion as a separately required, trusted workflow or ruleset that is loaded from outside the pull request's candidate tree, and execute a pinned validator/controller implementation there.

findings.failure_path: DEFAULT_PATHS binds only skills and .github. After a valid review, the branch can add or modify a root Makefile, repository script, configuration, or any other tracked path outside those directories; the recomputed candidate remains identical, the existing ledger still matches, and the additional unreviewed content reaches the same merge.
findings.smallest_fix: Hash every tracked landing change except a narrowly defined committed-evidence allowlist, or fail when the pull request contains paths outside the reviewed scope so those changes must be reviewed separately.
